newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore government securities steady to higher.
newsitem.headline: Singapore government securities steady to higher.

text.p: Singapore government securities were steady to higher in moderate trade on retail and interbank interest, dealers said on Wednesday.

"The interbank rate eased slightly again today but there was still little impact on the market. Treasury bill yields and bond prices were steady to slightly higher. Volume was moderate," a local dealer said.

"The market was pretty quiet today and most people were sitting on the sidelines, hesitant to open or hold new positions ahead of the May Day holiday tomorrow. But we might see some trade on Friday when the market reopens," another dealer said.
In treasury bills, three-months closed at a yield of 1.49/1.44 percent compared with Tuesday's yield of 1.45/1.40 percent but one-year was unchanged from Tuesday's yield of 1.60/1.55 percent.

Among bonds, April 1999 ended at S$99.60/99.65 against Tuesday's close of S$99.58/99.63, September 2001 was unchanged from Tuesday's S$96.89/96.94 and June 2003 ended at $S94.90/94.95 versus S$94.89/94.94.
The interbank rate eased slightly to 3-3/8 3-1/4 percent against Tuesday's 3-7/16 3-5/16 percent.
